title: End of the Bronson band; King Oliver takes over
summary: Phillips recalls Bronson's last dance at Christmas 1931 and King Oliver taking over the band in about March 1932 through the Frederick Brothers agency.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: What month of '31 did you stay with him til?
Up in Wichita, until King took the band over.
King Oliver took over Art Bronson's band.
Yeah. He took it over round about March of '32.

No, it must have been '32, because '31 we was still with Bronson. That's when they was arguing about what they was gonna do. Bronson wanted to know whether we... That's when King was after the band. He already had
He wanted to take over the band.

Yeah. So Bronson left, I think, around about... I remember the last dance we played under Bronson was Christmas -- Christmas of '31. The Christmas Holidays of '31. Then a guy named Tiny Taylor that sang with the band, he took it out for a while. He was going to sing with King's band anyway. So they got some dates, and Frederick Brothers... This was a big booking agency that was in Wichita. Frederick Brothers was booking King's other band, and he heard this band... They was telling him, "King, take this band. We want (?) to have this band." See, the band that we had, that last band we'd had was a much better band than the one King had when he had Freddie Moore and Paul Barnes and Clyde Bernhardt.
They were in King Oliver's band before you joined.
